istrazivacki-centar.html:
Research center



The Ministry of Security of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the University College "CEPS - Center for Business Studies" Kiseljak have established a Research Center in the field of protection and rescue (hereinafter: the Center) within the framework of mutual cooperation. The center is established as an expert, analytical, development and educational organizational unit within CEPS, without the status of a legal entity. The center acts as professional and analytical support to the Ministry of Security of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the areas of protection and rescue, disaster risk management, education and capacity development.

The Center is being established to:
• development and improvement of scientific and research work in the field of protection and rescue,
• development of strategic and planning documents based on risk assessments,
• improving the training and professional development system,
• connecting the academic community, institutions and operational practice,
• development of international cooperation and exchange of knowledge,
• support for the implementation of EU standards and international frameworks in the field of protection and rescue.

The Center can perform the following activities:
• preparation and implementation of scientific-research projects
• organization of conferences, seminars, workshops and professional meetings,
• preparation of analyses, risk assessments and expert reports,
• development of risk management methodologies and models,
• development of educational programs and training,
• development of digital tools and information systems,
• cooperation with domestic and international institutions,
• other activities agreed upon between the Parties.

The Center participates in the development and implementation of a system of education and professional training in the field of protection and rescue. As part of its activities, the Center can:
• develop training programs,
• organize Training of Trainers (ToT) programs,
• organize lifelong learning programs and specialist courses,
• develop modules for crisis management, DRR, CIMIC, STRATCOM and NICS,
• conduct training needs analyses,
• participate in the evaluation and standardization of training programs.

In accordance with the needs of the Ministry of Security of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the scope of work of the Center can be extended to other tasks and activities within the competence of the Ministry.

The Center can participate in:
• activities of the EU Civil Protection Mechanism,
• the work of the EU Civil Protection Knowledge Network
• international projects and research,
• expert exchange and education programs.

alerrt.title: ALERRT
alerrt.html:
CEPS – ALERRT CENTER (Texas State University)

Under a cooperation agreement with the ALERRT Center at Texas State University (United States of America), College "CEPS - Centar za poslovne studije" Kiseljak jointly launched specialist training programmes for police officers and law enforcement agencies.

The programme aims to provide law enforcement professionals with a simple, standardised set of skills to save as many lives as possible when responding to an active attacker incident, whether acting alone or as part of a small ad hoc team.

Participants also acquire the skills needed to provide emergency assistance at an attack site. They can then quickly and safely move critically injured casualties to a location where EMS personnel can provide advanced medical care and transport them to a clinical centre. EMS means Emergency Medical Services and includes medical technicians, ambulance staff and other healthcare professionals trained to provide emergency care. Their role is to respond rapidly, provide first aid, stabilise patients and transport them to hospitals or medical centres for further treatment.

NOTE: This training programme has been adopted and incorporated into FBI (Federal Bureau of Investigation) training and recognised by the United States Congress. More than one million participants and users have completed the training to date.

CEPS is authorised by the ALERRT Center at Texas State University to deliver the following modules through ALERRT-certified trainers in Bosnia and Herzegovina:
✔️ ALERRT Level 1 Training - 16 hour course.
✔️ ALERRT Level 1 Training - Undergraduate course - 3 credit college course.
✔️ Civilian Response to Active Shooter Events (CRASE) - 4 hour course.

crase.title: CRASE
crase.html:
CRASE (Civilni Resursi za Aktivnu Sigurnosnu Edukaciju)

The CRASE training programme prepares schools, institutions and companies by informing and training individuals and groups to AVOID a dangerous environment, DENY an attacker the opportunity to cause harm and DEFEND themselves when all other options have been exhausted. The course also teaches basic first aid, trauma care and lifesaving skills to support an injured person until medical professionals arrive.

The CRASE course prepares participants to:

• Understand civilian behaviour during an active attack.

• Teach the key safety principles: Avoid, Deny, Defend.

• Deliver standardised presentations and community training.

• Adapt training to local settings and needs while maintaining programme integrity.

On successful completion, each participant is certified to deliver CRASE training in their local community, creating a sustainable, locally led network of trainers.

CRASE is a civilian training programme from the accredited ALERRT Center at Texas State University, USA. ALERRT (www.alerrt.org) has supported law enforcement training in all 50 United States, reaching more than 400,000 emergency responders through over 20,000 courses: https://www.avoiddenydefend.org/

The CRASE train-the-trainer programme comprises four (4) hours of active instruction.

Participants who successfully complete CRASE train-the-trainer training may train others and encourage them to enrol in the train-the-trainer programme to support communities in need.

The programme is designed to provide public-service knowledge free of charge to end users. Implementation in Bosnia and Herzegovina is beginning through the accredited training centre at College "CEPS – Centar za poslovne studije" (www.ceps.edu.ba).

projekt/core-ed-academy.html:
Project title:
Fostering Inclusion and Shared Values in Juvenile Justice through Correctional Pedagogy and Specialist Professionalization, Empowered by the 'LiberateSkills' Correctional

Acronym:
CORE-ED ACADEMY

Funding:
ERASMUS-EDU-2024-CBHE-STRAND-2 (101179359)

Duration:
36 months (2025–2028)

Abstract:
This project strives to elevate the capabilities of higher education institutions in Albania, Bosnia Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, and Serbia. It aims to equip specialists with the skills to implement dynamic interventions that foster inclusion and common values in correctional settings, thereby supporting democracy and the rule of law. This unique partnership, a fusion of public-private initiatives, brings together education, the labor market, enterprises, research hubs, and the learner's perspective. It seeks to redefine higher education institutions as lifelong learning hubs, benefiting not only students but also working professionals. The introduction of two pioneering curricula in correctional pedagogy, a first in the European space, focuses on equipping learners with 'pedagogy-first' interventions. This multidisciplinary approach integrates law, psychology, social sciences, and education, dynamically benefiting children and youth in contact with the law. The project employs three key methodologies for success: DACUM approach workshops engaging employers and the labor market to identify current and foresight competencies; structured public hearings involving civil society, researchers, and public authorities to establish 5 Balkan Research Centres for Correctional Pedagogy joining the “LiberateSkills” Pact for Skills; and peer learning & mentoring between higher education staff from Western Balkan countries and two additional Balkan nations (Romania and Greece). This collaborative effort aims to develop regionally targeted research that is tailored to Balkan contexts, needs, cultures, and socio- political settings.

Project objectives:
1. SO1: To develop a co-production methodology for the HE institutions to coordinate in developing accurate and adapted Joint Correctional Pedagogy Ecosystem and a new Correctional Pedagogy Competencies Strategy including policy recommendations and "CORE-ED ACADEMIA" practices to support the HE sector growth and resilience at a National and regional level .
2. SO2: To update the existing and emerging Occupational Profiles present in the juvenile justice with new competencies by building an understanding of the principles of pedagogy-first in correctional settings; .
3. SO3: to foster innovation by providing new Joint Training Schemes and modern Recognition Systems under the form of 2 HE courses, one for bachelor level students studying relevant and connected disciplines identified and one for professionals as further education post-bachelor short form HE education.
4. SO4: To improve the research base and the conditions for excellence in research by providing opportunities for academia to connect with correctional state authorities and civil society, but also to provide students and correctional professionals facilities to drive local based research initiatives in juvenile justice.
5. SO5: To enhance the capacity of Education Providers and Correctional Representatives to co-create Correctional pedagogy ecosystems in juvenile justice-related training and to develop more tailored Curricula and Up-Skilling opportunities that could support the development of the sector.
6. SO6: To bring together all the Education Actors (Training Companies, VET providers, HEIs, correctional facilities and civil society) with the market representatives and umbrella associations in order to achieve a greater impact.
7. SO7: To raise the quality of HE provision and the attractiveness of the correctional sector at a European, National, Regional and Local Level.

KVCs become centres for entrepreneurship, digital transformation and inclusion, aligned with the European Green Deal, Digital Europe and the EIT HEI initiative.

The project strengthens university capacities through tools and infrastructure for technology transfer, interdisciplinary cooperation and the development of entrepreneurial strategies aligned with the Smart Specialisation Strategy (S3) at local and European levels. It places particular emphasis on including marginalised groups, including women, young people, veterans and people with disabilities, in innovation and entrepreneurship.

By 2027, IMPACT-Campus will train 950 students and 365 staff members, supporting digital leadership and sustainable EU growth. projekt/ncp_widera_net.title: (NCP_WIDERA.NET) Widening Participation and Strengthening the European Research Area
projekt/ncp_widera_net.html:
Project title:
Widening Participation and Strengthening the European Research Area

Acronym:
NCP_WIDERA.NET

Funding:
HORIZON-WIDERA-2021-NCP-IBA

Duration:
36 months (2025–2028)

Abstract:
NCP_WIDERA.NET is a European support network for National Contact Points (NCPs) working within WIDERA, part of the EU Horizon Europe framework programme for research and innovation. It coordinates and connects NCPs responsible for WIDERA across Europe. NCPs provide guidance, information and support to universities, research institutes, companies and other organisations seeking to participate in Horizon Europe projects. The network strengthens NCP capacities to help institutions prepare competitive proposals and find international partners.

Project lead for Bosnia and Herzegovina:

  • Visoka škola “CEPS-Centar za poslovne studije” Kiseljak (Bosnia and Herzegovina);

 

National Contact Point for WIDERA in Bosnia and Herzegovina:

  • dr. Mirzo Selimić

 

Support:

  • dr. Nermin Palić

 

Activities:

The WIDERA framework supports several types of activity, including:

  • Twinning projects which strengthen research cooperation between institutions.
  • Teaming projects focused on establishing or improving centres of excellence.
  • ERA Chairs, which bring leading researchers to institutions in widening countries.
  • Hop-on facility, which enables partners from widening countries to join existing Horizon Europe projects.
  • Capacity-building activities for NCPs through networks such as NET.

 

Structure:

Overall project structure NCP_WIDERA.NET is divided into 9 work packages (WPs) to be implemented over the 36-month project duration. The work packages aim to deliver the planned results and impacts and include the following:

  • WP1 „Proposal pre-check“ aims to support NCPs and potential applicants in widening countries through two main objectives:
    1. reducing the innovation gap by enabling NCPs in widening countries to rapidly acquire knowledge and experience of NCP systems developed in other countries, through a Proposal Precheck Guide, training and capacity-building activities;
    2. raising awareness of activities intended to increase the visibility of qualified potential applicant organisations from widening countries.
  • WP2 „Matchmaking“ targets potential applicants from widening countries as well as applicants from non-widening countries (advanced partners). Its main purpose is to promote participation by widening actors in calls under Pillar II, and help advanced partners find consortia for widening actions using various partnering tools and platforms.
  • WP3 „Widening NCPs capacity building“ aims to improve and professionalise NCP services through training on key technical issues in the widening programme and mentoring new NCPs through introductory training and webinars.
  • WP4 „Widening stakeholders and synergies“ aims to connect relevant stakeholders to ensure synergies between Widening and other programmes and initiatives. It targets programme owners, managing authorities and NCPs of other programmes such as ESIF, EEN, COST, EIT and others.
  • WP5 „ERA sharing for NCPs“ informs the ERA NCP network about specific European Research Area issues and evaluates how project activities improve NCP services. Activities map the expertise, good practices and needs of all NCPs to share existing knowledge through training, study visits and peer learning. The aim is to improve and professionalise the support provided by NCPs.
  • WP6 „ERA visibility for clients“ aims to increase the visibility of the ERA programme component among potential applicants. Clients will receive activities and tools to improve their understanding of ERA and support successful project participation.
  • WP7 „Communication“ targets WIDERA NCPs and relevant stakeholders to raise awareness of project activities and the new roles and services of Widening NCPs, including proposal prechecks. It will also increase the visibility of WIDERA within Horizon Europe and promote success stories, strengthening the reputation of applicants from widening countries.
  • WP8 „Advancing Europe Package support“ focuses on implementing elements of Advancing Europe Package (AEP), in particular proposal pre-check services and partner matchmaking activities.
  • WP9 „Management“ aims to ensure successful project management, including information exchange among partners and efficient coordination of all project activities.

projekt/skill-2-sustain.title: (SKILL2SUSTAIN) Boosting digital and green skills for a resilient and sustainable Western Balkan society
projekt/skill-2-sustain.html:
Project title:
Boosting digital and green skills for a resilient and sustainable Western Balkan society

Acronym:
SKILL2SUSTAIN

Funding:
ERASMUS-EDU-2024-CBHE-STRAND-2 (101178204)

Duration:
36 months (2025–2028)

Abstract:
Boosting digital and green skills for a resilient and sustainable Western Balkan society – SKILL2SUSTAIN is fully aligned with the objectives of the CBHE action, the activities, and the specificities of Strand II. The urgent need for the Western Balkans to accelerate the twin green and digital transition has been recognized through analysis conducted in the target countries of Region 1. The broader aim of the project is to mainstream a holistic approach to digitalization and the green transition, while its specific objectives are in line with the EU Green Deal, the Digital Education Action Plan 2021–2027, and the Council Recommendation on learning for the green transition and sustainable development. The project supports higher education systems in creating green and digital societal ecosystems. A Digital and Green Initiative for WBC Education in Academia will be developed and signed by all project partners. Over three years, 10 curricula will be modernized or newly developed and implemented across 5 WBC HEIs: 2 new BSc programs in Disaster Risk Management, 3 modernized BSc/MSc programs, and 5 new certified LLL programs. These will introduce innovative green topics such as circular economy, energy efficiency, renovation wave, climate change adaptation, sustainability, disaster resilience, and digital skills in Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS). The modernization and development paths will be defined based on national and regional needs, supported by know-how transfer from EU HEIs. Furthermore, 5 educational ICT-based interoperable Research and Education Centers will be established at WBC HEIs. Teaching methodologies will be enhanced through study visits, and blended learning materials will be offered in EN/ALB/MNG/BIH/SRB via an ICT collaboration platform and an open-access e-library.

Project objectives:
1. SO1: Establish Research and Education Centres (RECs) for the green and digital transition at each participating Western Balkan higher education institution.
2. SO2: Raise awareness among staff and students of the need for green and digital skills in higher education institutions.
3. SO3: Promote a culture of green transition and digitalisation within Western Balkan higher education institutions.
4. SO4: Increase synergies between academia and relevant stakeholders through joint green transition and digitalisation initiatives.
5. SO5: Strengthen networks and cooperation between Western Balkan and EU staff and student communities in digitalisation and green transition activities.

Project title:
Skills and Employment Enhancement in Green Logistics

Acronym:
SEE-GL

Funding:
ERASMUS-EDU-2024-CB-VET (101181098)

Duration:
24 months (2025-2027)

Abstract:
Skills and Employment Enhancement in Green Logistics (SEE-GL) aims to revitalise vocational education and training (VET) in transport logistics in Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo and Montenegro by integrating environmental, social and governance (ESG) principles. The initiative addresses environmental impact, social inclusion and governance challenges in a logistics sector essential to regional economic development and alignment with European standards. By developing a unified VET curriculum incorporating ESG principles, SEE-GL aims to equip professionals with the skills needed for sustainable logistics operations. The project emphasises cooperation between the private and public sectors and the use of digital educational tools to ensure broad access and participation. This approach aims to modernise logistics, making it more inclusive and responsive to market needs. SEE-GL focuses on strengthening VET institutions, aligning programmes with labour market needs and integrating local, regional and national development strategies. A key result will be a new generation of ESG transport logistics professionals ready to address industry challenges with sustainable solutions. The project aligns with Erasmus+ objectives of inclusion, digital transformation and international cooperation. Its commitment to ESG principles and strategic approach to vocational education support sustainable logistics development in the Western Balkans. By building skills and promoting sustainable practices, SEE-GL aims to contribute to regional economic growth and environmental sustainability.

Project objectives:
1. Build the capacities of VET providers to strengthen private–public cooperation in vocational education and training, delivering market-oriented interventions based on available opportunities;
2. Improve the quality and adaptability of vocational education and training to economic and social changes, increasing the relevance of skills to labour market needs;
3. Align vocational education and training with local, regional and national development strategies.
